title: Formulas, Weights, and Methodology
subtitle: Complete technical documentation on Wizdam Impact Score (WIS) computation, SDG classification, API integration, and the Sangia Scieco architecture patterns.

wis.intro: The Wizdam Impact Score is a composite 0–100 score measuring the real-world impact of a researcher or research output across four dimensions:
wis.src_social: Media mentions, policy citations, public engagement
wis.src_sdg: Alignment with the 17 UN SDGs (via Sangia AI)

academic.intro: Computed by the Sangia API Engine based on:
academic.d_hindex: Number of h works with at least h citations each
academic.d_i10: Number of works with at least 10 citations
academic.d_recency: Higher weight for citations in the last 5 years
academic.d_network: Breadth of the international collaboration network

social.intro: Entered manually or via crawler for each researcher:
social.d_media: Mentions in news media or blogs
social.d_altmetric: Impact on academic social media (ResearchGate, Academia)

economic.d_adoption: Adoption of research results by industry
economic.d_patents: Patents citing or based on the researcher's work
economic.d_startups: Startups born out of the research

sdg.intro: The SDG score is derived from how strongly a researcher's whole body of work aligns with the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals.
sdg.d_causal: Weight of causal linkage to an SDG
sdg.d_min_rel: Minimum score to be categorized relevant
sdg.d_high_rel: Score threshold for the “Highly Relevant” label

data.intro: To save API quota and reduce latency, Wizdam Scola sends data it already holds in the database to the Sangia API (supplied_data), so Sangia doesn't need to re-fetch it from ORCID/Scopus.

batch.intro: For long-running computations (many works), the Sangia API uses a batch pattern:
batch.retry_note: Retry up to 3× on HTTP 410 (session expired)
batch.sleep_note: Sleep 300ms between requests to avoid rate limiting

crawler.n_semantic: Use an API key for a higher quota
